title: WPMS/2003/2012 of NIKHIL MITTAL Vs U.K. STATE MATSYA PALAK VIKAS ABHIKARAN and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION NO. 2003 OF 2012 (M/S)
Nikhil Mittal ÖÖ..Petitioner.
Versus
Uttarakhand State Matsya Palak Vikas Abhikaran
and others Ö.Respondents.
Present: Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Additional Chief Standing Counsel
for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Manoj Tiwari, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Alok
Mehra, Advocate for respondent no. 5.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.(Oral)
1. Rejoinder affidavit filed in Court today is taken on
record.
2. Heard Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary, Advocate for the
petitioner, Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Additional Chief Standing
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand and Mr. Manoj
Tiwari, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Alok Mehra,
Advocate for respondent no. 5.
3. The petitioner before this Court was one of the
bidders for the fishing rights in ìNanak Sagar Damî for
which an advertisement for auction was published on
10.8.2012 and the bid was to be open on 31.8.2012. The
petitioner being the highest bidder who gave a bid to the
tune of `1,37,55,888/- was to be given the fishing rights.
As per the conditions of the tender notice, the petitioner

2
had to deposit 25 % of the bid amount which the
petitioner had deposited on the same day. The matter
was sent to the State Government by the tender
Committee. All the same, the petitioner received an order
dated 18.9.2012 (Annexure No. 1 to the writ petition) of
the Deputy Director (Administration), Directorate of
Fisheries by which it was said that since there were
objections raised by other bidders regarding his character
certificate and the matter was referred to the State
Government, the proposal which was sent in his favour
has been rejected by the State Government and hence his
contract has been cancelled. It is this order which the
petitioner has challenged before this Court.
4. The counter affidavit has been filed by the State
Government wherein it has been stated that the
petitioner did not fulfill one of the mandatory conditions
which was filing of character certificate along with bid
documents. Since it was a mandatory condition, his bid
stood disqualified and the petitioner comes in the
category of disqualified bidders and his bid was not liable
to be considered.
5. The fact of the matter remains that the bid of the
petitioner was not only considered but it has been stated
in the minutes of the meeting of the Committee that the
bids were opened on 31.8.2012 for fishing rights in
ìNanak Sagar Damî and out of 7 bids which were
received, the petitioner was the highest bidder whose bid
was of `1,37,55,888/- However, certain bidders have
raised objections regarding character certificate of the
petitioner. The petitioner had given a character certificate
issued by a Station House Officer i.e. by a police

3
authority whereas the character certificate was to be
given by the District Magistrate. All the same, the
certificate given by the police authority was considered to
be enough and thereafter his bid was considered. Since
the bid of the petitioner was highest he was directed to
deposit 25 % of the bid amount. This shows that not only
the petitioner was the highest bidder (in fact this fact has
been admitted by the respondents) but there was an
approval by the authorities as regarding his character
certificate. Since there was still some doubt regarding the
character certificate given to the petitioner, the petitioner
in any case submitted his character certificate on
11.9.2012.
6. The only question remains before this Court for
consideration is as to whether the submission of the
character certificate by the petitioner is a mandatory
condition and in absence of character certificate his bid
was liable to be rejected. The fact of the matter is that not
only the bid of the petitioner was considered, he remains
the highest bidder with a bid amount of `1,37,55,888/-.
He had given the character certificate issued by a Station
House Officer which was considered by the authority to
be enough. Moreover, the terms and conditions of the
tender notice though stipulate that in the absence of the
character certificate the bid will not be considered, it is
an admitted case that the bid of the petitioner was
considered and found to be the highest. Therefore, in
view of this fact, even if there was a condition for filing a
character certificate, this stood waived by the Committee.
Therefore, in all fairness, the contract is liable to be given
to the petitioner.

4
7. Writ petition therefore succeeds and is hereby
allowed. Order dated 18.9.2012 (Annexure No. 1) to the
writ petition is hereby quashed. A mandamus is issued to
the Deputy Director (Administration), Directorate of
Fisheries, Dehradun to execute the contract in favour of
the petitioner.
8. No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
5.10.2012
Avneet
